Subject: SKU decision heuristic and fallback rules for Dedicated reservations (Orion.ai)

Leah — thanks again for the sync this morning. As promised, I sketched a pragmatic heuristic you can use to translate your workload signals into a Dedicated GPU mix and reservation sizing. Attaching a short workbook that walks through the arithmetic and a checklist for tradeoffs. [Attachment: 20280611-orion-sku-heuristic-sheet.xlsx]

Top-level recommendation pattern (short):
- If model/context requirements need >80GB host-visible memory or models >70B parameters w/ KV/cache sizing, prefer H100 reservations (memory-first).
- If throughput is the primary constraint with short context (<=2k tokens) and high QPS, L4 is the cost-efficient default (throughput-per-dollar).
- A100 sits in the middle: best-for when you need moderate memory (~40–80GB effective) and predictable FP16/AMP perf with familiar tooling.

Heuristic (decision tree):
1) Start with workload inputs: steady QPS, peak concurrency, average & p95 context length, model family/size, soft latency SLO p95.
2) Memory gate: if (model_size + kv_cache_per_request) * concurrency > available_memory_per_gpu * 0.7 -> move to larger-memory SKU (A100->H100).
3) Latency gate: if p95 latency target < 150ms and workload is low-batchable -> favor lower-latency SKUs (A100 or H100 depending on memory), avoid large batching on L4 unless caching reduces work.
4) Cost gate: if predicted token-cost delta of H100 > 1.6x A100 without clear perf win, prefer A100+quantization or L4 for batchable paths.

Sizing rules and headroom guidance:
- Reserve at least 20% headroom above estimated steady-state concurrency for burst tolerance.
- Add cache instances (L4 or A100) dedicated to KV/prefix caching to offload repeated context.
- For mixed models, reserve a small H100 pool for heavyweight finetuned models and autoscale L4 for passthrough static workloads.

Operational fallbacks:
- Region/zone fallback: route non-sensitive inference to lower-cost region if capacity constrained.
- Model fallback: define an A/B rollback to a quantized variant of the same model when H100 capacity hits >85% utilization.

Questions for you to confirm (so we can finalize proposal):
- Expected steady QPS and peak concurrency numbers (per-minute peaks).
- Typical and max context length (tokens).
- Latency SLO (p95) and whether you accept best-effort for p99.
- Any procurement limits on initial SKU selection (e.g., H100 not allowed).

Next steps: I’ll incorporate your numbers into the attached workbook and return a two-option quote: (A) Aggressive headroom (H100-heavy) and (B) Cost-optimized hybrid (A100 + L4).

Thanks,

Naomi — nice write-up, a couple of operational points I want to flag for the proposal:

- Memory safety margin: bump the 0.7 factor to 0.75 for workloads that use dynamic KV cache growth (we've seen runtime growth when LLM plugins call external tools).
- Quantization ops: call out potential 4-bit quantized pathways (with L4/A100) for non-sensitive embeddings/generation. That can reduce H100 needs by ~25% in our model estimations.
- Cache sizing: recommend adding 1 dedicated L4 per ~200 concurrent users for prefix caching when you have high repetition.

Operational rollout suggestion:
- Canary: 2 H100s + 4 A100s + 6 L4s in a private VPC in us-east-1 for initial 2-week smoke test. Route 5–10% of traffic to the canary; monitor p95 latency and token cost.

I'll let Naomi and Karthik incorporate these into the workbook; we should also include a clear fallback path in the SOW (rolled capacity swap to A100-based variants).

Vivek
VP, Product Ops — Redwood Inference

Naomi — this is very helpful, thank you. A few constraints from our side before you finalize:

- Procurement is pushing back on H100 across the board for initial commitments due to budget restrictions; they want a primarily A100/L4 mix unless we can justify H100 for a narrow class of models.
- Our forecast (next 12 weeks): steady QPS ~2,800, peak concurrent requests ~1,200 (5-minute peak). Typical context length ~3.8k tokens, p95 latency target 120ms (we can tolerate p99 degradation up to 300ms during bursts).
- We have one heavy analytics model (private, 70B-ish) that currently uses 60–70GB effective memory with KV caching. We want that isolated to the smallest H100 pool if used.
- Security: deployment must be in our private VPC in us-east-1 and meet our audit log requirements (SOC2 evidence already requested by procurement). See attached MRP doc. [Attachment: orion_mrp_requirements.pdf]

Please send a 2-option firm sizing and a short note on expected monthly cost delta between options. Also include a 45-day canary/rollback timeline and suggested monitoring playbooks (what metrics we'll watch and thresholds).

Leah — thanks for the numbers and constraints. Based on your forecast and the internal comments above, here's a concise two-option proposal and the rationale so procurement has clear tradeoffs. Attached is the updated workbook with the calculations. [Attachment: 20280611-orion-sku-heuristic-sheet.xlsx]

Option A — Conservative (cost-optimized hybrid, recommended initial):
- Reserved: 40 A100 (effective memory configuration: 80GB partitioning)
- Burst/Autoscale: 120 L4s for high-throughput paths and caching
- H100: 4 reserved units (narrow pool) dedicated to the 70B analytics model only
- Headroom: ~22% steady-state headroom above 5-minute peak after autoscale ramps
- Rationale: A100 covers memory needs for most models; L4 handles low-latency high-QPS traffic cost-effectively; small H100 pool keeps heavy model isolated for predictable performance.

Option B — Performance-lean (latency/SLA-first):
- Reserved: 60 A100
- Burst/Autoscale: 80 L4s
- H100: 8 reserved units for lower tail latency on heavy models and headroom during peak events
- Headroom: ~35% steady-state headroom
- Rationale: larger A100 reserve reduces risk of cross-sku fallthrough, raising p95 headroom and reducing runtime model swap frequency.

Estimated monthly delta (approx):
- Option A baseline cost estimate: $XX,XXX/month (license + infra) — breakout in workbook
- Option B delta: ~+28–35% on infra line items vs Option A, driven by H100 and additional A100 reservations. Exact numbers in workbook based on your contract term.

Canary & rollout plan (45 days):
- Week 0: Deploy canary in private VPC (2 H100 / 6 A100 / 10 L4), run 5–10% traffic routing, validate p95/p99 and audit logs.
- Week 1–3: Expand to 20–40% traffic if metrics stable.
- Week 4–6: Full traffic migration and validation; adjust autoscale thresholds and caching sizes.
- Rollback: automated routing back to A100-quantized variant and throttle ingress if p95 breaches 150ms for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.

Monitoring playbook (short):
- Core metrics: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization by SKU, KV cache hit ratio, token cost per minute.
- Alerts: p95 > 150ms (sev2), p99 > 300ms (sev1), H100 utilization > 85% for >10 minutes (capacity trigger).

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred option and contract term (12 vs 36 months) so we can firm pricing.
2) We’ll deliver a formal SOW with SKU counts, SRE runbook, audit evidence checklist within 3 business days of confirmation.

If procurement still objects to H100, Option A can be revised to replace H100 with A100 + quantized variant at some additional latency risk for the heavy model — I'll include that alternate tab in the workbook.

Thanks — attaching the workbook and MRP mapping links.
